notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 27 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 8 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: The source uses different amounts of native register-pair arithmetic.
notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: Including reachable helpers reverses the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.
